title: Ephemeral Prompt Approval and Rollback — Scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Experimenting with 'ephemeral prompts' feature: user-supplied prompt blobs that can be temporarily attached to a session for augmentation, tools, or experimental completions. They are short-lived (minutes-hours) and often come from non-privileged UIs (extensions, sandboxed widgets).
- Need lightweight approval and rollback semantics to: prevent leakage of sensitive system instructions, enable quick revocation if prompts misbehave, and provide an audit trail for compliance.

Goals: 
- Fast approval path: allow autopermit for low-risk prompts (heuristics).
- Human review lane: escalate suspicious prompts to CS/Trust reviewers.
- Atomic attach/detach: operators can rewind sessions to pre-attach state or apply compensating actions.
- Low perf overhead: approval checks should add <5ms median to happy-path requests.

Constraints & non-goals:
- Not building a full policy engine (Oso/PDP) yet — just heuristics + review queue.
- Ephemeral prompts are NOT persisted beyond TTL unless explicitly promoted.
- Minimal changes to client SDK; prefer server-side enforcement.

Proposed Flow (happy path):
1) Client POST /sessions/{id}/ephemeral-prompts with prompt blob + metadata (origin, risk-tags).
2) Runtime applies quick heuristic checks (token length, banned-phrase list, entropy check).
3) If pass -> issue ephemeral-attach token, attach to session state V+1, emit audit record, return 200 + token.
4) Prompt active until TTL or explicit detach.

Escalation flow (suspicious):
1) Heuristic flags -> create RDW-5148 review ticket and put prompt into review-queue (async).
2) Temporarily attach in 'shadow' mode: preview outputs are marked and not surfaced to end-users until approved.
3) Reviewer accepts -> convert to normal attach; rejects -> issue revoke and optionally rewind affected sessions.

Rollback semantics (operator reversion):
- Two modes: soft-detach (stop using prompt for new completions) and rewind (recompute outputs or mark outputs as tainted).
- Minimal instrumentation: each completion has metadata: session_id, prompt_attach_version, prompt_sha, attached_at. That lets us identify affected tokens/answers.
- Rewind strategy: for short sessions (<=3 responses) we can recompute by re-running with previous attach_version; for long sessions, provide a 'taint' flag in Console and an export of affected exchanges for manual remediation.

State machine (ASCII):
[submitted] --(heuristic pass)--> [attached:active v1] --(TTL)--> [expired]
         \                     
          --(heuristic flag)--> [under_review] --(approve)--> [attached:active v2]
                                 |--(reject)--> [revoked]

Operational notes:
- Attach token: HMAC(sid|version|expiry) signed by runtime KMS key. Support key-rotation.
- Audit log: append-only in Console stream. Include reviewer id, decision, reason, ticket id. Retain 365 days for enterprise customers.
- Metrics: time-to-attach, % auto-approve, review queue depth, mean time-to-review, rollback requests/day.

Integration points:
- Console: review UI, search by prompt_sha, one-click revoke/rewind, bulk export.
- Rollouts API: when promoting ephemeral -> permanent prompt (promote across tenants), create a model/variant tag.
- Dedicated/private differences: private deployments should default to stricter heuristics and send telemetry back via partner agent only (or not at all) — need opt-in.

Edge cases & tradeoffs:
- Rewind nondeterminism: some model outputs are nondeterministic; rewinding might not recreate original outputs. Keep original outputs + taint flag for auditability.
- Performance vs safety: heavy static analysis reduces auto-approve rate. Start conservative then relax with data.
- Abuse surface: attackers may chain ephemeral prompts to exfiltrate; heuristics should include rate limits per origin and per tenant.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Should review queue run in a separate bounded worker pool to avoid head-of-line blocking? (Action: prototype)
- Q2: Exact schema for prompt metadata (risk-tags, source-app, fingerprinting). Draft a proto. (Ben)
- Q3: UX for users when their prompt is in 'shadow' mode — show clear provenance. (Lina)
- Q4: Rewind policy for enterprise SLAs: allow replay vs mark-as-tainted — default? (Product)

Prototype next steps:
- Minimal server-side impl: attach token + audit record + simple banned-phrase list (2d).
- Console mock: review card + revoke/rewind button (3d).
- Telemetry: add metrics to runtime telemetry pipeline (1d).
- Wire a small E2E with sandbox client to validate performance (perf bench, 5000 small prompts).

Notes to self: keep schema lightweight. Capture examples of prompts that should be auto-approved vs reviewed to tune heuristic thresholds. File examples -> GH gist for training review heuristics.

References & quick links:
- RDW-5148: review queue epic
- Runtime PR draft: runtime/pull/2321
- Slack thread: #trust-safety ephemeral-prompts (link pinned in RDW-5148)

---
This is a working scratchpad — rough, expects iteration. Will extract into a short RFC once prototype results in metrics.
